results.title: Ajinkya Shinde to lead CJP's protest after Dipke's detention
results.description: New Delhi, Oct 10 (IANS) Following the detention of the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) core leadership on Saturday, founder Abhijeet Dipke handed over the charge of the outfit's protest against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, to CJP's Organisation In-Charge Ajinkya Shinde. Hours after the CJP chief, along with co-conveners Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained from a flight at the Indira Gandhi International (IGI) Airport in Delhi, Dipke's X handle posted a video in which he is heard asking supporters to now follow Ajinkya Shinde's leadership who will head the CJP's protest in the absence of the conveners. "If you are watching this video, it means that I, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka have been arrested. In our absence, Ajinkya will lead the protest and the CJP movement. All those of you who are watching this video please follow Ajinkya Shinde. He will be carrying forward the Cockroach Janta Party after Ashutosh, me and Saurav," Dipke said in the pre-recorded video. Earlier, Delhi Police personnel entered the aircraft carrying Dipke after it landed at IGI Airport. Custom Ad: Multiplex Dipke posted the video showing the Delhi Police team entering the flight as he, along with other CJP members, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, were detained from the flight itself. In a video posted on his social media handle, Dipke was heard telling the police, "...I have come here to be arrested; arrest me." The CJP announced the detentions in a post on its social media handle, stating: "Abhijeet Dipke DETAINED! Saurav Das DETAINED! Ashutosh Ranka DETAINED!" Social media influencer Dhruv Rathee was also detained from his residence in Gurugram. According to a post on the X handle of the CJP, around 50 police personnel in plain clothes reached Rathee’s residence in Gurugram at around 8 a.m. and took him into custody. Moreover, according to officials, around 1000 protesters have been detained from different parts of the national Capital on Saturday, while on their way to take part in the agitation called by the CJP to demand CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over alleged irregularities in the conduct of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Meanwhile, Abhijeet Dipke's grandmother passed away on Saturday in Santuk Pimpri village of Maharashtra’s Hingoli district. She had been unwell for the past few days due to a prolonged illness and age-related ailments. According to Delhi Police, Dipke has been informed about the unfortunate demise of his grandmother. Officials said that it is now up to Dipke whether he wants to stay back to continue the protest under detention or return for the last rites. --IANS cg/rad

results.title: Congress slams restrictions in Delhi over CJP protest, says democracy being 'muzzled'
results.description: New Delhi, Oct 10 (IANS) The Congress on Saturday criticised restrictions imposed in Central Delhi over the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) protest at Jantar Mantar, alleging that the Union government was curbing citizens' fundamental rights and suppressing dissent. Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge and senior party leaders Shashi Tharoor and P. Chidambaram condemned the security measures, including alleged detentions, restrictions on movement and disruptions to public transport and internet services. Kharge, in a post on social media platform X, said, "Our youth, students, lawyers, journalists, social activists, farm union leaders, YouTubers, content creators, everyone who is questioning this regime (BJP government) are being detained. Modi Govt has turned the 'Mother of Democracy' into a 'Muzzled Democracy'." "The cowardice of the BJP-RSS is on full display today. Detentions, arrests, jails, lathis and pellets cannot deter the people of India. Since the days of our freedom struggle, the youth have been at the forefront of shaping the nation's destiny. The Congress Party, along with the united Opposition, will fight this tyrannical regime, tooth and nail," he added. Custom Ad: Multiplex Kharge said that the Congress would continue to defend democracy, the Constitution and the fundamental rights of every Indian. Congress MP Shashi Tharoor also expressed concern over the security arrangements in the national capital, citing checkpoints, concrete barriers, spike strips and a heavy deployment of police and paramilitary personnel. Tharoor said he had returned to Delhi after 2 a.m. and had rarely witnessed such extensive restrictions in the city. He also referred to reports of train cancellations, metro station closures and young people being detained from their homes and streets in and around Delhi. He alleged that the measures were intended to prevent citizens from peacefully questioning the integrity of elections. He also criticised the reported suspension of internet services in parts of the national capital. "Freedom of movement stands completely shackled. Jantar Mantar was designated precisely so that citizens could voice dissent in the centre of Delhi, and today even the roads leading to it have been declared out of bounds," Tharoor said. He questioned the deployment of security personnel and asked why similar urgency was not demonstrated when women in the national capital required protection. Tharoor demanded the release of those detained and questioned whether authorities would impose similar restrictions if protesters returned on October 12. "Our GenZ deserves better than an undeclared Emer-GenZ," he said, adding that a government confident in the fairness of elections should welcome questions rather than respond with restrictions. He also said that barricades would not restore public confidence in the Election Commission and urged the Union government to provide answers instead of using force against protesters. "The strength of a democracy is measured by how it treats those who question its working, and by that measure, what we have seen today is utterly shameful and unconscionable," Tharoor added. Senior Congress leader P. Chidambaram also criticised the restrictions, alleging that the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) was going to extraordinary lengths to protect the Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. He claimed that the closure of Metro stations, deployment of police personnel from other states, internet shutdowns and restrictions on peaceful protests had disrupted the lives of ordinary citizens. "The youth are protesting; their minds are protesting; their hearts are protesting; their families are supporting them. And they are the voters in the next election," Chidambaram said. He added that the BJP would eventually realise that suppressing dissent and denying fundamental rights was not the way to win or retain power. --IANS jk/khz
